outputs.L1: A method and apparatus for manufacturing a press component without causing cracks in a flange on the inner circumferential side of a curved portion involve free-bending press working of a blank made of an ultra-high-tensile-strength steel sheet. The press component is manufactured by cold-press working the blank. During press working, a material-inflow-facilitating portion is provided near the region of the blank to be formed into the flange on the inner circumferential side of the curved portion. This portion increases the flow of material from the region of the blank to be formed into an end portion of the press component into the region to be formed into the flange.
outputs.L2: A technique and device are provided for producing a pressed component from an ultra-high-tensile-strength steel-sheet blank by cold free-bending press forming, while preventing cracks in a flange located along the inner circumference of a curved section. During forming, a material-inflow-promoting region is created near the blank area intended to become the inner-circumferential flange. This region increases the flow of material from the blank section that will form an end of the pressed component into the section that will form the flange.
outputs.L3: The method manufactures a pressed component from an ultra-high-tensile-strength steel sheet. During production, a blank is cold-pressed using a free-bending technique. To prevent cracks from forming in the flange along the inner circumferential side of a curved portion, a material-inflow-facilitating portion is created near the area of the blank that will become the inner flange. This feature promotes the flow of material from the portion that will form the end of the component into the future inner flange, thereby reducing localized strain and minimizing the risk of cracking during the pressing process.
outputs.L4:
A press component having a curved section and an inner circumferential flange can be manufactured from an ultra-high-tensile-strength steel blank by cold free bending. Before or during press forming, a material-inflow facilitating portion is provided in the blank near the region that will form the inner circumferential flange. The facilitating portion may be configured as a local relief, bent portion, bead, recess, or other shape that reduces resistance to movement of the sheet material and supplies additional material to the flange-forming region.

During free bending, the blank is drawn and deformed along the curved section. Because the inner circumferential side has a relatively short forming path and is subjected to severe tensile strain, insufficient material inflow can cause excessive thinning or cracking, particularly when ultra-high-tensile-strength steel is used. The material-inflow facilitating portion allows material from an adjacent region of the blank to move more readily toward the inner circumferential flange as forming progresses. This distributes strain, suppresses localized thinning, and prevents the flange edge or its vicinity from fracturing.

The facilitating portion is positioned and dimensioned so that it promotes the required inflow without impairing the final shape or strength of the component. It may remain in a noncritical area of the finished part, be flattened in a subsequent forming operation, or be removed during trimming. The method can therefore form complex curved press components at room temperature without relying on hot pressing or extensive intermediate operations.

By improving material supply to the inner circumferential flange, the method reduces forming defects and variation between parts. As a result, press components made from ultra-high-tensile-strength steel can be manufactured reliably while retaining the weight-saving and strength advantages of the material.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize a patent describing a method for cold press-forming an ultra-high tensile strength steel sheet while preventing cracks in the inner flange of a curved portion.
counterfactuals.output:
The patent addresses cold press-forming ultra-high tensile-strength steel into a component having a curved section and an inward-facing flange, where conventional forming tends to cause stretch-flange cracking.

Its method uses staged forming rather than producing the final geometry in one stroke. The blank is first formed into an intermediate shape that controls material flow and limits tensile strain at the inner flange of the curve. A subsequent pressing step brings the wall and flange to their final angles and dimensions. By distributing deformation between the stages—and avoiding excessive edge stretching or localized strain—the process suppresses cracking without hot forming or major loss of dimensional accuracy.

The method enables lightweight, high-strength automotive structural parts with curved, flanged profiles to be manufactured using ordinary cold-press equipment.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: What manufacturing method can prevent cracking in an inner circumferential flange when producing a curved press component from ultra-high-strength steel?
counterfactuals.output: Use a **multi-stage press-forming process** rather than forming the curved flange in one stroke. First preform the region that will become the inner circumferential flange—often with a temporary bulge, bead, or enlarged bend radius—to create reserve material. Then form the curved body and finally restrike/flatten the flange to its finished shape. This staged material feed reduces circumferential tensile strain and prevents stretch-flange cracking in ultra-high-strength steel.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for a method and apparatus that uses free bending and a material inflow facilitating portion to manufacture crack-free press components.
counterfactuals.output: A method and apparatus for manufacturing a press-formed component from a sheet material are disclosed. The method includes positioning the sheet material between a die and a punch, initiating deformation of the sheet material by free bending while permitting at least a portion of the sheet material to remain unsupported, and subsequently press-forming the sheet material into a target shape. During deformation, a material inflow facilitating portion provided in at least one of the die, the punch, or a blank holder reduces resistance to movement of the sheet material toward a forming region. The free bending and facilitated material inflow suppress excessive tensile strain and local thinning in crack-prone regions, thereby enabling manufacture of a crack-free component, including components having high curvature or formed from high-strength or low-ductility materials. The apparatus includes the die, the punch, and the material inflow facilitating portion, which may comprise a recessed, inclined, curved, low-friction, or selectively movable surface configured to control material flow during forming.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain how modifying blank material flow near an inner flange can reduce cracking during cold press working of ultra-high tensile strength steel sheets.
counterfactuals.output:
Cracking at an inner flange is usually caused by severe **stretch-flange deformation**. As the flange is raised, its cut edge must lengthen circumferentially. Ultra-high tensile strength steel has limited edge ductility, so localized tensile strain—especially near sheared-edge defects—can quickly produce cracks.

Cracking can be reduced by controlling blank flow so that more material is supplied to the high-strain flange region instead of forcing the edge itself to stretch. This can be done by:

- changing the blank outline or adding local material allowance near the flange,
- reducing blank-holder restraint or draw-bead resistance in the material-supply direction,
- increasing restraint elsewhere to redirect flow toward the inner flange,
- using relief cuts, optimized corner radii, or staged forming to distribute deformation.

With appropriate flow control, material moves inward from the surrounding sheet, reducing circumferential edge strain, strain concentration, thinning, and tensile stress at the flange root and edge. The deformation is spread over a larger area, keeping local strain below the steel’s fracture limit. Excessive inflow must still be avoided because it can cause compression, wrinkling, or flange-shape errors.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention for manufacturing a curved press component in which material is encouraged to flow from an end-forming region into the inner circumferential flange region.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention is a press-forming method and die set for producing a curved component having an inner-circumferential flange, where material shortage would otherwise cause flange cracking or excessive thinning.

A sheet-metal blank is placed between a punch, die, and selectively controlled blank holder. During forming, the area that forms an end of the component is restrained less strongly—or is provided with surplus material—than the remaining peripheral area. As the tools close, this end-forming region is drawn toward and into the region forming the flange on the inside of the curve. Draw beads, local holder clearances, movable pads, or independently controlled holder forces may be used to guide and regulate the flow.

After sufficient material has entered the inner-flange region, the component is finish-formed and, if necessary, trimmed or calibrated. By supplying material from the end region rather than forcing the inner flange to stretch excessively, the process reduces cracking, thinning, wrinkling, and dimensional error while allowing tighter curvature and higher-strength sheet materials to be used.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
